verdictStatement: Both claimed repairs are sound and both of the dispatch's named attacks fail. dependencyGraph no longer claims to own layer assignment; it cites ID-DEP-K2 and hands the L-TCB boundary to DR-126, and lEvalPublication resolves the L-EVAL case I raised by reservation rather than by silence. The alias-edge exception is gone, both duplicate cases fail unconditionally, and the replacement reservation sets a six-part bar for a later owner — it even closes the filesystem-alias versus independent-equal-content-files case my own advisory had missed. The closed roster holds at 23 changed paths with zero escapees, and v4 restored the universal sentence v3 had dropped, so the claim is falsifiable again. I paid particular attention to HEAD moving to 8fdd59c between versions: file 08 is byte-identical across the move so the row pin still resolves, D-106 leaves all four reverified decisions untouched, and reMeasurementAtV4's three values and its narrative of what moved are exactly right. What fails is smaller than any previous round and sits entirely in the succession metadata. notFoldedThisSuccessor declares my v3 ADV-1, ADV-2, ADV-4 and ADV-5 to be honesty residue. Measurably, ADV-1, ADV-4 and ADV-5 were fully folded — the universal sentence restored, the v1 verdict pin restored, the live remeasurement added — and ADV-2 was half folded by the HISTORICAL prefix. Only the duplicated guidance line is genuinely residue. honestyRepairsFromV3 omits the three performed repairs to match. The direction is benign, the successor did more than it claimed, but the field a coordinator reads to learn what is outstanding currently names three finished items as unfinished. The adjacent Claude-v2 declaration is accurate, which is what makes this a discrete slip rather than a wording preference, and the fix moves three lines between two rostered fields without touching a rule, a pin or a verbatim string.
